chapters.title: Weigh Our Sins in the Balance
chapters.html:
Ezra Sutuel 3

The First Vision: Ezra's Complaint

1In the thirtieth year after the ruin of our city I was in Babylon, I, Sutuel, who am called Ezra. I was troubled as I lay on my bed, my face was downcast, and my thoughts rose up in my heart,

2because I saw the desolation of Zion and the joy of those who lived in Babylon.

3My spirit was greatly troubled, and I began to speak words of fear to the Most High.

4I said, "O Lord God, did You not speak in the beginning, when You created the earth, and that by Yourself alone, and commanded the dust,

5and it brought forth Adam in a mortal body? He too was the work of Your hands, and You breathed into him the breath of life, and he became alive before You.

6You led him into paradise, which Your right hand had planted before the earth was established.

7You gave him a righteous commandment, and he transgressed it; and then You appointed death for him and for his generations. From him were born nations and peoples, tribes and clans without number.

8Every nation walked by its own will and sinned before You, and You did not stop them.

9Again, in its time, You brought a flood on the earth and on those who lived in the world, and destroyed them.

10Their judgment was alike: as You brought death on Adam, so You brought the flood on these.

11Yet You left one of them, Noah, with his household, and from him came all the righteous.

12Then, when those who lived on the earth began to multiply and increase, and their children were multiplied, and peoples and nations were born of them, they began again to sin more than those before them.

13When they had sinned before You, You chose for Yourself one of them, whose name was Abraham.

14You loved him, and to him alone You showed the end of the time, when you two were alone by night.

15You made an everlasting covenant with him, that You would never forsake his seed. You gave him Isaac, and to Isaac You gave Jacob and Esau.

16You set Jacob apart for Yourself, but Esau You put aside; and Jacob became a great multitude.

17When his seed went out of Egypt, You brought them to Mount Sinai.

18You bowed the heavens and shook the earth, You troubled the world, You made the deep tremble and stirred up the sea.

19Your glory passed through four gates, of fire and of earthquake, of wind and of hail, to give a law to the seed of Jacob and a commandment to the family of Israel.

20Yet You did not take the evil heart away from them, so that Your law might bear fruit in them.

21For the first man, Adam, clothed himself with an evil heart, and he transgressed and was overcome; and not he alone, but all who were born of him.

22So the sickness remained, with Your law, in the heart of the people, together with the evil root; and the good passed away, and the evil remained.

23The days passed and the years were completed, and You raised up for Yourself a servant whose name was David.

24You told him to build a city for Your name and to offer in it from what is Yours.

25This went on for many days and years. Then those who lived in the land sinned,

26doing nothing different from what Adam and all his generations had done, for they too had clothed themselves with the evil heart.

27So You handed Your city over to Your enemies.

28Then I said in my heart that day, 'Do those who live in Babylon do any better, that they should take the city of Zion?'

29But when I came here, I saw sins without number, and my soul saw many who had denied You. These thirty years my heart has been astonished

30at how You bear with sinners and spare the ungodly, and have cast off Your people and preserved Your enemies;

31and You have not told anyone at all where this way will end. Does Babylon do better than Zion?

32Or has any other nation known You besides Israel? Or what people has believed in Your law as Jacob has,

33whose reward has not appeared, and whose labor has borne no fruit? I have gone among the nations and found them rejoicing, though they do not remember Your law or Your commandments.

34Now weigh in the balance our sins and the sins of those who live in the world, and see on whose side even a little turns the beam of the scale.

35When have those who live in the world not sinned before You? Or what nation has kept Your commandments like this?

36You may find individual men by name who have kept Your commandments, but a nation that is perfect You will not find."

Notes

  • The book — Ezra Sutuel is the book other Bibles call 2 Esdras 3–14 (4 Ezra), and its chapters and verses are numbered as theirs are; the Ethiopic book begins here, at chapter 3. It is rendered from the Ethiopic as Richard Laurence translated it into English (1820) from one manuscript, compared with Dillmann's edition of the Ethiopic (1894, from ten manuscripts) and with the Latin and the Syriac. Where Laurence's manuscript lacks words, they are kept from the other witnesses: Noah, with his household (v11), which Dillmann's edition also has; Isaac, Jacob and Esau (vv15–16) and individual men by name (v36), from the Latin and the Syriac, where Dillmann's edition has a gap.

  • v1 "I, Sutuel, who am called Ezra" — the Ethiopic gives him the name Suta'el; the Latin has Salathiel, the Syriac Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2; 1 Chronicles 3:17). The book gives Ezra this second name.

  • v14 "to him alone You showed the end of the time" — the Latin and the Syriac read the end of the times, the close of the ages. Laurence's English of his manuscript has the termination of his life, his Latin finem temporis ejus, the end of his time. The end of the time leaves both readings open.

  • vv20–22 "You did not take the evil heart away from them… the evil root" — the question the whole book asks begins here. Genesis says the shaping of the human heart is evil from his youth (Genesis 8:21). The law was given, but the evil heart was not taken away, and so the law could not bear its fruit.

chapters.title: The Forest and the Sea
chapters.html:
Ezra Sutuel 4

Uriel's Three Questions

1Then the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered me

2and said to me, "Your soul is utterly bewildered. Do you think you can find out the counsel of the Most High?"

3I said, "Yes, my lord." He answered me, "I have been sent to show you three ways and to set three likenesses before you.

4If you can explain one of them to me, I too will show you the way you long to see, and teach you why this evil exists."

5I said, "Speak, my lord." He said to me, "Go, weigh the fire in a balance, measure the wind with a measure, or call back for me the day that has passed."

6I answered, "Who born of a woman can do this, that you should ask it of me?"

7He said to me, "If I had asked you, 'How many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs at the face of the deep, or how many ways above the heavens? Which is the way to Sheol, or which the way to paradise?'

8you would surely have said to me, 'I have never gone down into the deep, I have never gone down into Sheol, and I have never gone up into heaven.'

9But now I have asked you only about the fire and the wind and the day that has passed, and you have no answer to give me about them."

10He said to me, "If you cannot understand what passes away,

11how can you understand the ways of the Most High? The ways of the Most High are formed beyond all reckoning, and you who are corruptible cannot understand the ways of Him who is incorruptible." When I heard this, I fell on my face

12and said, "It would have been better for us never to have been created than, once created, to live in sin and suffering and not know why we suffer."

The Forest and the Sea

13He answered me, "The forest and the trees of the plain went and took counsel together,

14saying, 'Come, let us go and make war on the sea, so that it may give way before us, and we may make ourselves another forest.'

15In the same way the waves of the sea took counsel together and said, 'Come, let us go up and make war on the forest of the plain, so that there too we may make ourselves another country.'

16But the counsel of the forest came to nothing, for a fire came and consumed it.

17So did the counsel of the waves of the sea, for the sand rose up and stopped them.

18If you are wise in judgment, tell me: which of them would you acquit, and which would you condemn?"

19I answered, "Each of them took a foolish counsel, for the land was given to the forest, and the sea a place to bear its waves."

20He answered me, "You have judged rightly. Why then have you not judged so in your own case?

21For as the land was given to the forest and the sea to its waves, so those who live on the earth can understand only what is on the earth, and not Him who is in heaven, nor what is in heaven."

22Then I answered, "I beg you, my lord, why then were we given a mind to understand?

23I did not want to ask about the ways above, but about what passes before us every day: why Israel has been given over to the nations, the people He loved to a sinful people; why the law of our fathers has been brought to nothing, and the written covenant is nowhere.

24We pass away from the world like locusts, our life is like smoke, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.

25What then will become of His holy name, by which we are called? These are the things I have asked."

The Harvest Has Not Come

26He answered me, "If you remain, you will see, and if you live, you will know the times; for the world is hastening to pass away.

27It cannot bear what is hoped for the righteous, for it is a world full of sorrow and sickness.

28The evil you asked me about has been sown, but its harvest has not yet come.

29Unless what was sown is reaped, and the place where the evil was sown passes away, the field where the good is sown will not come.

30For a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and the fruit of sin has grown from it and increased until now, and will grow until its harvest comes.

31Consider for yourself: if one grain of evil seed has brought so great a crop of sin,

32when good seed is sown beyond counting, how great a harvest it will yield!"

33I answered him, "How long, and when will this be? For our days are few and evil."

34He answered me, "Do not be in more haste than the Most High. You are in haste for your own sake alone, but the Most High for the sake of many.

35Did not the souls of the righteous ask about this in their chambers, saying, 'How long are we to be here? When will the harvest of our reward come?'

36Jeremiel the angel answered them, 'When the number of those like you is complete. For He has weighed the world in the balance,

37and measured the sea with a measure; and He will neither command silence nor speak until the measure set for it is fulfilled.'"

38I answered, "O Lord, my Lord, we are all full of sin.

39Perhaps it is because of us that the harvest of the righteous is held back, because of the sins of those who live in the world."

The Womb and the Earth

40He answered me, "Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when she has completed her nine months, her womb can keep what is in it any longer."

41I said, "It cannot, my lord." He said to me, "Sheol and the dwellings of the spirits of the righteous are like the womb.

42For as the womb hastens to give birth in its pain, so the earth hastens to give back from its womb those who have been in it since the creation of the world.

43Then all that you long to see will be shown to you."

44I answered, "If I have found favor in your sight, and if it is possible,

45tell me whether the days still to come in this world are more than those that have passed, or whether more have passed;

46for what has passed I know, but what is to come I do not know."

47He said to me, "Stand at the right side, and I will show you the meaning of a likeness."

48I stood and looked, and a blazing furnace passed before me; and when the flame had gone by, I looked, and smoke remained.

49After this a cloud full of water passed before me and poured down a heavy and violent rain; and when the force of the rain had passed, drops remained.

50He said to me, "Consider for yourself: as the rain is more than the drops, and the fire more than the smoke, so the measure of what has passed is far greater; what is left is drops and smoke."

51Then I pleaded with him, "Will I live until those days? What will happen in those days?"

52He answered me, "About what you ask me, I can tell you in part; but about your life I was not sent to tell you, and I do not know it."

Notes

  • v1 "the angel… whose name was Uriel" — the angel 1 Enoch names first among the holy angels who watch: Uriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the world and over Tartarus (1 Enoch 20:1–2), the angel of its book of the heavenly lights. Here he answers Ezra's questions about the ways of the Most High.

  • vv29, 37, 41, the witnesses — Laurence's manuscript and Dillmann's edition break off in v29 before the field where the good is sown will not come, which the Latin and the Syriac have; it is kept. In v41 Sheol, in Dillmann's edition, the Latin and the Syriac, is kept, though Laurence's manuscript lacks it. In v37 the Ethiopic has measured the sea, where the Latin and the Syriac have measured the times.

  • v33 "our days are few and evil" — Jacob's words to Pharaoh, Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life (Genesis 47:9).

  • vv41–42 "the earth hastens to give back from its womb those who have been in it" — the resurrection pictured as birth. 1 Enoch says the same of the last day: the earth will give back what was entrusted to it, and Sheol will give back what was entrusted to it (1 Enoch 51:1).

chapters.title: One Vine, One Dove, One People
chapters.html:
Ezra Sutuel 5

The Signs of the End

1"As for the signs: the days are coming when great terror will seize those who live on the earth. The way of truth will be hidden, and the land of faith will be barren.

2Wickedness will increase beyond what you have seen and what you have heard.

3A land that you now see ruined and laid waste will rule, and the earth will become a desert.

4If the Most High lets you live, you will see the earth thrown into confusion after the third time, and the sun will suddenly shine by night and the moon by day.

5Blood will drip from wood, and the stone will utter its voice, and the peoples will be in turmoil,

6and the stars will fall from their courses. One whom many do not expect will reign,

7and all will hear his voice.

8There will be an uproar in many regions, fire will burst out again and again, the wild beasts will leave their own country, and women will give birth to monsters.

9Water that is sweet will be found bitter, and friends will suddenly fight one another. Wisdom will hide herself in that day, and understanding will return to her chamber,

10and many will seek her and not find her; and wickedness and lawlessness will increase on the earth.

11One region will ask its neighbor, 'Has righteousness, or anyone who does what is right, passed through you?' And it will answer, 'No.'

12In those days people will hope and not obtain, they will marry and not rejoice, they will toil and labor, and their way will not prosper.

13These are the signs I have been sent to tell you. If you pray again and weep as you do now, and fast seven days, you will hear greater things than these."

14Then I awoke. My body shook violently, and my soul was so troubled that it fainted.

15But the angel who had come to speak with me took hold of me, strengthened me and set me on my feet.

Phaltiel and the Fast

16On the second night Phaltiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said, "Where have you been, and why is your face so sad?

17Do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the land of their exile?

18Get up, then, and eat some bread, and do not abandon us, like a shepherd who leaves his flock in the power of cruel wolves."

19I said to him, "Go away from me, and do not come near me for seven days; then come back to me." He listened to what I said and left me.

20I fasted seven days, mourning and weeping, as the angel Uriel had commanded me.

The Second Vision: The One and the Many

21After the seven days the thoughts of my heart troubled me greatly again,

22and a spirit of understanding lifted up my soul, and I began once more to speak before the Most High.

23I said, "O Lord, my Lord, from all the forests of the earth and from all its trees You have chosen for Yourself one vine;

24from all the lands of the world You have chosen for Yourself one land;

25from all the depths of the sea You have filled for Yourself one river; from all the cities that have been built You have set apart Zion for Yourself alone;

26from all the birds that were created You have set apart for Yourself one dove; from all the flocks that were made You have chosen for Yourself one sheep;

27and from all the many nations of the earth You have chosen for Yourself one people, and to this people, whom You loved above all, You gave the law You approved out of all laws.

28Now, O Lord, why have You given up the one to the many, and dishonored the one root more than the others, and scattered Your few among the many?

29Those who believe in Your law are trampled by those who oppose Your covenants.

30If You hated Your people, they should have been punished by Your own hand."

A Circle of Judgment

31When I had spoken these words, the angel who had come to me the night before was sent to me,

32and he said to me, "Listen to me, and I will teach you; pay attention to me, and I will tell you more."

33I said, "Speak, my lord." He said to me, "Are you greatly troubled for Israel? Or do you love Israel more than his Maker does?"

34I said, "No, my lord. I spoke out of grief, for my inmost being torments me every hour as I try to find the way of the Most High and to understand the path of His judgment."

35He said to me, "You cannot." I said, "Why, my lord? Why then was I born? Why did my mother's womb not become my grave, so that I would not have seen the travail of Jacob and the exhaustion of the race of Israel?"

36He said to me, "Count for Me the days that have not yet come; gather for Me the scattered drops; make the withered flowers green again for Me;

37open for Me the shut chambers, and bring out for Me the souls shut up in them; show Me the faces of those you have never seen, and let Me hear their voices; and then I will tell you about the suffering that has rightly come upon them."

38I said, "O Lord, my Lord, who can know these things, except one whose dwelling is not with mortals?

39As for me, I am simple and lowly. How could I speak of what You ask me?"

40He said to me, "As you cannot do one of the things I have named, so you cannot find out My judgment, or the end of My love, for which I wait patiently for the sake of My people."

41I said, "O Lord, my Lord, You have waited patiently for their sake. But what will become of those who were before us, and of us, and of those who come after us?"

42He said to me, "I liken My judgment to a circle: as there is no slowness for the last, so there is no haste for the first."

43I answered, "Could You not have created at one time those who have been, those who are, and those who are to come, so that You might show Your judgment sooner?"

44He answered me, "The creation cannot hasten ahead of its Creator, and the world cannot hold all at once those who are created in it."

chapters.title: Through the Son of Man
chapters.html:
Ezra Sutuel 6

Before the World Was Made

1He said to me, "Its beginning was through the Son of Man, and its end will be by Me alone. For before the earth and its regions were made, before the ways of the world stood firm, before the winds blew,

2before the sound of the thunder was heard, before the flash of the lightning shone, before the foundation of paradise was laid,

3before the fair flowers were seen, before the powers of movement were established, before the hosts of angels were numbered,

4before the heights of the air were raised up, before the measures of the heavens were named,

5before the trace of the years to come was known, before the schemes of those who now sin were set aside, and before those who store up faith were sealed,

6then I took thought, and it was by Me alone, and not by another."

7I answered, "What will be the sign of its time? When will the first age end, and when will the other world begin?"

8He said to me, "From Abraham to Isaac, for from him were born Jacob and Esau.

9Esau is the end of this age, and Jacob is the beginning of the world that follows.

10For the end of a man is his heel, and his beginning is his hand. Seek nothing further, Ezra."

The Voice Like Many Waters

11I answered, "O Lord, my Lord, if I have found favor in Your sight,

12show Your servant the end of Your signs, part of which You showed me last night."

13He answered me, "Rise and stand on your feet, and you will hear a mighty, sounding voice.

14If the place where you stand shakes violently

15while it speaks with you, do not be terrified, for the word concerns the end. The foundations of the earth will understand

16that it speaks of them, and they will tremble and shake, for they know that their end must be changed."

17When I heard this, I rose and stood on my feet and listened, and a voice spoke, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.

18It said, "The days are coming when I will draw near to visit all who live on the earth,

19when I will search out those who have done wrong by their wickedness, and when the humiliation of Zion is complete,

20and when the age that is passing away is sealed. This is the sign I will give: the books will be opened before the face of heaven, and all will see Me together.

21Children a year old will speak with their voices, and pregnant women will give birth to infants of three and four months, and they will live and be raised up.

22Land that seemed unsown will appear sown, and full storehouses will be found empty.

23The trumpet will sound, and all who hear it will suddenly be terrified.

24In those days friends will fight against friends like enemies; the earth and those who live on it will be terrified, and the springs of water will stand still and not flow for three hours.

25Whoever is left of all those I have told you of will live, and will see My salvation and the end of My world.

26On that day they will see the men who were taken up and have not tasted death since their birth. The heart of those who live in the world will be changed, and they will be given another heart.

27For evil will be blotted out, and deceit will be extinguished.

28Faith will flourish, corruption will be overcome, and the truth, which has gone so long without fruit, will be made known."

29While he was speaking to me, little by little the place where I stood began to shake.

30He said to me, "I have come to show you these things, as on the night before.

31If you pray again and fast again seven days,

32I will tell you again greater things than these; for your voice has been heard before the Most High, and He has seen the uprightness you have kept from your youth.

33That is why He sent me to show you all these things, and to say to you, 'Take courage, and do not be afraid,

34and do not hurry to dwell on vain thoughts about the former times, that you were not born in the last days.'"

The Six Days

35After this I wept again in the same way and fasted seven days, to complete the three weeks he had told me of.

36That night my heart was troubled within me again, and I began once more to speak before the Most High,

37for my spirit burned within me, and my soul was in distress.

38I said, "O Lord, my Lord, You spoke at the beginning of creation, on the first day, and said, 'Let heaven and earth be made,' and Your word did the work.

39Your Spirit was hovering over all, and within, all was darkness and silence; the sound of a human voice was not yet.

40Then You commanded that light come out of Your treasuries, so that Your works might appear.

41On the second day You created the spirit of the firmament and commanded it to divide the waters, so that one part might go up and the other part remain below.

42On the third day You commanded the waters to be gathered into the seventh part of the earth, and six parts You left dry, so that in them people might plow and sow and live before You.

43Your word went out, and at once the work was done.

44Fruit came forth without number, of every taste and kind; flowers of many colors, trees of many sorts and many fragrant scents. This was done on the third day.

45On the fourth day You commanded the light of the sun and the light of the moon to be, and the stars in their order,

46and You commanded them to serve man, who was about to be formed.

47On the fifth day You told the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, to bring forth living creatures, birds and fish.

48The mute and lifeless water brought forth living creatures, so that the generations might tell of Your glory.

49Then You kept two living creatures that You had created; the one You named Behemoth, and the other You named Leviathan.

50You separated them from each other, for the seventh part, where the water was gathered, could not hold them both.

51To Behemoth You gave one of the parts dried up on the third day, to live in it, where the mountains are.

52To Leviathan You gave the seventh part, the watery one; and You have kept them to be food for whom You will.

53On the sixth day You commanded the earth to bring forth before You cattle, beasts and creeping things,

54and over all these You set Adam as ruler over all the works You had made before; and because of him we, Your people whom You chose, are overwhelmed.

55All this I have spoken before You, O Lord, because You said that You created the world for our sake.

56As for the other nations, born of Adam, You said that they are nothing; they are like froth, like a drop from a bucket, and their joy is nothing.

57And now, O Lord, these nations that are counted as nothing rule over us and trample us.

58But we, Your people, whom You called 'My firstborn, My only one, My beloved,' have been handed over into their hands.

59If the world was created for our sake, why do we not possess our world as our inheritance? How long will this go on?"

Notes

  • v1 "Its beginning was through the Son of Man, and its end will be by Me alone" — so the Ethiopic, as Laurence's English and the shape of Dillmann's edition give it, and the Syriac, The beginning was through the Son of Man, but the end is through my own hands. The Latin lacks the clause. It answers Ezra's question in 5:56, through whom You will visit Your world. Laurence's English reads on account of the Son of man. The title is Daniel's one like a son of man who came with the clouds of heaven (Daniel 7:13), and 1 Enoch's Son of Man who has righteousness (1 Enoch 46:3).

  • vv8–10 "Esau is the end of this age, and Jacob is the beginning… his heel… his hand" — the twins' birth, his hand holding the heel of Esau (Genesis 25:26): Esau came out first, and Jacob followed with his hand on Esau's heel, so the age that ends and the age that begins touch. The Ethiopic says From Abraham to Isaac, the Latin and the Syriac From Abraham to Abraham. v9's first clause, Esau is the end of this age, where Laurence's manuscript and Dillmann's edition break off, is kept from the Latin and the Syriac, as are v5's schemes of those who now sin.

  • vv49–52 "Behemoth… Leviathan" — the two great beasts that close the book of Job (Job 40–41). 1 Enoch tells of the same separation: a female monster named Leviathan, to live in the depths of the sea… and the male, named Behemoth, in a wilderness east of the garden (1 Enoch 60:7–8).

  • v58 "whom You called 'My firstborn, My only one, My beloved'" — the word Moses was to say to Pharaoh, Israel is My son, My firstborn (Exodus 4:22).

chapters.title: O Adam, What Have You Done?
chapters.html:
Ezra Sutuel 7

The Narrow Way

1After I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been with me on the nights before was sent to me again.

2He said to me, "Rise, Ezra, and hear the words I have come to speak to you."

3I said, "Speak, my lord." He said to me, "There is a sea set in a wide place, broad and boundless;

4but its entrance is set in a narrow place, no wider than a river.

5If anyone wants to see the sea, how can he reach its broad expanse unless he passes through the narrow entrance?

6Here is another likeness: a city is built on a plain, full of every good thing;

7but its entrance is narrow and set on a cliff, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left,

8and only one path between them, between the fire and the water, so narrow that it holds the footsteps of only one person.

9If this city is given to someone as an inheritance, how will he receive his inheritance unless he passes through the danger set before it?"

10I said, "So it is, my lord." He said to me, "So it is with the land of My Israel and their inheritance,

11for I made the world for their sake. When Adam transgressed My statutes, the ways of this world became rough and narrow;

12they became few and evil, full of every kind of trouble, toil and hardship.

13But the ways of the other world are great, wide and glorious, and they bear immortal fruit.

14Unless the living pass through this rough and futile road, they cannot receive what is stored up for them.

15Why then are you troubled, you who are dust? Why are you so disturbed, you who are mortal?

16Why have you not set your mind on what is to come, as well as on what is now?"

17I answered, "O Lord, You have ordained in Your law that the righteous will inherit these things, but the ungodly will perish.

18The righteous endure what is narrow, hoping for what is wide; but the ungodly trust in what is narrow, and they will never see what is wide."

19He said to me, "There is no judge above God, and no one with understanding above the Most High.

20Let the many perish who disregard the law He set before them.

21For God strictly commanded those who came into the world what they should do to live, and what they should keep to escape punishment.

22But they would not be persuaded, and they spoke against Him; they devised vain things for themselves,

23and set deceit and wickedness before themselves; and on top of all this they said, 'There is no God.'

24They forsook His ways, scorned His law, despised His covenant, disbelieved His statutes and neglected His works.

25That is why empty things are for the empty, and full things for the full.

The Messiah and the Judgment

26For the time is coming when the signs I have foretold to you will appear: the city that now appears will be hidden, and the land that is now hidden will appear.

27Everyone who has been delivered from the evils I foretold will see My glory.

28For My Messiah will be revealed with those who are with Him, and He will make those who have been raised up rejoice.

29After this My Child, My Messiah, will die, and all people who have breath.

30The world will be turned back to its ancient silence for seven days, as it was at the beginning, so that no one is left.

31After seven days it will be roused, and the perishable world will pass away.

32The earth will give up the bodies laid in it, and the dust those who rest in it, and then they will give back the souls entrusted to them.

33On that day the Most High will appear on the seat of judgment. His mercy will come, His compassion will cease, and His patience will come to an end.

34Only judgment will remain; truth will stand, faith will flourish,

35the work will follow, and the reward will be shown; righteousness will awake, and unrighteousness will not sleep.

36Then the pit of judgment will appear, and opposite it the place of rest; the furnace of Gehenna will be shown, and opposite it the paradise of joy.

37On that day the Most High will say to the people who have been raised, 'Look and understand whom you have denied, whom you would not serve, and whose commandments you have despised.

38Look on this side and on that: here is joy and rest, and there is judgment and fire.' So He will speak to them on the day of judgment.

39This is how the day of judgment will be: there will be neither sun nor moon nor stars,

40nor cloud nor thunder nor lightning, nor wind nor water nor sky, nor darkness nor day nor night,

41nor winter nor summer nor harvest, nor cold nor heat, nor mist nor hail nor frost, nor rain nor dew,

42nor evening nor dawn, nor brightness nor splendor nor blazing light; only the radiance of the glory of God, so that those who wait for Him may see all things in Him.

43That day will last as long as seven years.

44This is His judgment and His decree; to you alone have I shown these things."

Few Saved, Many Lost

45I answered, "Now I will call blessed those who keep Your commandments.

46But as for what I asked: who is there who does not sin, and who that is born has not transgressed Your statutes?

47I see now that the world to come will bring joy to few, but torment to many.

48For an evil heart has grown up in us, which leads us astray, brings us into ruin, and draws us into the way of death and the path of destruction, and takes us far from life; and not a few, but all who have been born."

49He answered me, "Listen to me, and I will speak to you and explain again

50why the Most High has made not one world but two.

51For you have said that the righteous are few, not many. Listen, then:

52make for yourself a vessel of lead and of potter's clay."

53I said, "How, my lord, can this be?"

54He said to me, "Not only this; ask the earth, and it will tell you and teach you.

55Say to it, 'You have brought forth gold and silver, bronze, iron, lead and potter's clay;

56but more silver than gold, more bronze than silver, more lead than iron, and more clay than lead.'

57Judge for yourself which is precious and desirable: what is plentiful, or what is rare?"

58I said, "O Lord, my Lord, what is rare is more precious, and what is plentiful is despised."

59He answered me, "You have judged rightly, for whoever has what is rare rejoices more than whoever has what is common.

60So also is the hope of the righteous, who are Mine. I will rejoice over the few who will live, because they will come to My glory, for in them My name has been glorified.

61I do not grieve for those who perish, for they are now like fire, like a flame and like smoke: they burn, they blaze, and they go out."

62I answered him, "O earth, what has become of the dust that shares your nature?

75I answered him, "If I have found favor before you, explain this to your servant: when we die and our soul goes out from each of us, will we be kept in a place of rest until the time comes when He establishes His judgment, or will we be judged from that very hour?"

  • The chapter and its numbering — vv36–105, from the pit of judgment to no one will ever be able to plead for another, are missing from the Latin text the King James Version was made from, so the King James has 70 verses here: it goes from v35 straight to Abraham's prayer (v106 here) and numbers on from 36. The Ethiopic and the Syriac have the whole chapter, and it is numbered as they and the restored Latin number it.

  • vv28–29 "My Messiah will be revealed… My Child, My Messiah, will die" — so the Ethiopic, as Laurence's English and the shape of Dillmann's edition give it. The Syriac has my son the Messiah and a reign of thirty years; the Latin has my Son Jesus and four hundred years, then my Son Christ shall die. The Ethiopic gives no number of years: the Messiah will make those who have been raised up rejoice, and after that He dies, with all who have breath, before the seven days of silence and the resurrection.

  • v118 "O Adam, what have you done? If you had not sinned, this evil would not have come upon us" — the Latin and the Syriac have your fall was not yours alone, but ours also who are descended from you.   • v129 "Choose life" — Moses' words, I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, so that you may live (Deuteronomy 30:19).

  • vv132–139 "merciful… compassionate… patient… abundant in mercy" — the names of the LORD proclaimed to Moses, God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love and truth (Exodus 34:6), taken one by one, each with its reason.

The Narrow Way

but its entrance is set in a narrow place, no wider than a river.
If anyone wants to see the sea, how can he reach its broad expanse unless he passes through the narrow entrance?
Here is another likeness: a city is built on a plain, full of every good thing;
but its entrance is narrow and set on a cliff, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left,
and only one path between them, between the fire and the water, so narrow that it holds the footsteps of only one person.
If this city is given to someone as an inheritance, how will he receive his inheritance unless he passes through the danger set before it?"
I said, "So it is, my lord." He said to me, "So it is with the land of My Israel and their inheritance,
for I made the world for their sake. When Adam transgressed My statutes, the ways of this world became rough and narrow;
they became few and evil, full of every kind of trouble, toil and hardship.
But the ways of the other world are great, wide and glorious, and they bear immortal fruit.
Unless the living pass through this rough and futile road, they cannot receive what is stored up for them.
Why then are you troubled, you who are dust? Why are you so disturbed, you who are mortal?
Why have you not set your mind on what is to come, as well as on what is now?"
I answered, "O Lord, You have ordained in Your law that the righteous will inherit these things, but the ungodly will perish.
The righteous endure what is narrow, hoping for what is wide; but the ungodly trust in what is narrow, and they will never see what is wide."
He said to me, "There is no judge above God, and no one with understanding above the Most High.
Let the many perish who disregard the law He set before them.
For God strictly commanded those who came into the world what they should do to live, and what they should keep to escape punishment.
But they would not be persuaded, and they spoke against Him; they devised vain things for themselves,
and set deceit and wickedness before themselves; and on top of all this they said, 'There is no God.'
They forsook His ways, scorned His law, despised His covenant, disbelieved His statutes and neglected His works.
That is why empty things are for the empty, and full things for the full.
